sub: Tension, your pace — always your call to skip.

1.name: Simmer
1.sub: Compliments, noticing, the pull you can't quite name yet.
q: On three, both say the exact moment tonight you started paying attention.~Whoever's came later explains what they missed.
Say one thing you find attractive about them that has nothing to do with how they look.
Guess the 'type' I'd never admit to on a first date.~Then I admit it, and you say whether you saw it coming.
Finish this out loud: 'I noticed you before you noticed me when—'
Guess the most attractive thing someone can do without trying, in my opinion.~Then I tell you — and whether you've done it tonight.
Tell them the detail of how they look tonight that you clocked first.~They aren't allowed to deflect it or say thanks for ten seconds.
On three, both name a compliment that does nothing for you.~Then both name the one that works every time. Don't use it yet.
Guess which thing you said tonight I'm still thinking about.~Two guesses. Then I just tell you.
What's something about them tonight that you didn't expect to find this attractive?
Say a compliment you'd believe instantly, however over the top.~Then they say it to you, properly, and you have to just take it.
What's the most honest reason you said yes to tonight — and if you're still deciding, that's a fine answer too.
Say the compliment you'd give if you knew it wouldn't go to their head.~Say it anyway. Risk it going to their head.
What's one thing about the way they laugh that you like more than you'd ever say out loud?
Guess what I'd order if you had to pick for me.~Then tell me why that guess is a compliment.
Name a deliberate thing you did tonight hoping they'd notice.~Then they say whether they noticed. No mercy.
Guess the thing about my voice that gets your attention.~Then I tell you the thing about yours.
What's something confident about them that you find more attractive than anything they could say?
Finish this out loud: 'Something I like about being near you is—'
Name a compliment you got once and still think about.~Then they decide whether to say it to you. They don't have to.
Tell them one thing you've wanted to say tonight but kept almost saying instead.
Guess the look I gave you tonight that you'd like to see again.~Then do it back to me and see whether I recognise it.
Both name the exact second the energy changed. On three.~Different seconds? One of you was slower. Work out which.
What's one thing about tonight that already feels different from a normal night out?
Say, plainly, one reason you're glad it's them sitting across from you right now.
What's a memory of them — from tonight or before — that you didn't expect to still be thinking about?
Does the way they say your name do anything to you?~They say it once, right now, before you answer. Then answer.
Guess what I noticed about your hands tonight.~Then I tell you. Then you look at mine.
Name one thing about the way they move through a room that you find more attractive than you'd say in front of other people.
Guess the thing you're wearing that I keep circling back to. One guess.~Then I point at it.
Complete this without planning it first: 'What gets me is the way you—'
What's a compliment about their mind you've been sitting on all night?
What's the quietest moment tonight that you actually liked the most?
Say the exact distance you'd want to be sitting from them. Plainly.~Neither of you moves yet. Just say it.
What's one thing about them you're genuinely curious to find out before the night's over?
Guess what they're like when nobody else is around to see it.~Then they tell you how close you got. Unedited.
What's a small thing they did tonight — probably without noticing — that you noticed completely?
Give them the compliment that's a little too honest to just be nice.~They don't get to laugh it off.
What's something about sitting close to someone warm that you like more than you'd admit out loud?
Their laugh, their eyes, or their hands. Pick one — no hedging.~Then defend it for thirty seconds while they listen without reacting.
What's the last thing about them tonight that made you want to keep looking?

2.name: Heat
2.sub: Real want now, out loud — teasing and tension both fair game.
q: Guess my physical tell for when I'm into someone.~Then tell me whether I've been doing it tonight.
Say the thing you'd tell a friend about tonight, in the voice you'd use.~Now say it straight to their face.
On three, both say where your mind actually went in the last ten seconds. Unedited.~Neither of you hears the other first.
What's the one thing keeping you from doing what you actually want to do right now?
Finish this out loud: 'The thing I'm trying not to think about right now is—'
Both name the moment the tension stopped being funny. On three.~Named different moments? The earlier one explains.
Describe, in one sentence, the exact kind of attention you're craving right now.
Describe the pull you're feeling right now without using the word 'want.'
Say the boldest true thing you're about to talk yourself out of.~Then they rate the boldness out of ten. Under five, go again.
Name the tone of voice that gets you every time.~Then they use it on their next sentence. You have to sit with it.
What's a thought you've had about them tonight that you immediately filed under 'later'?
Say the compliment that would fluster you if they said it back.~Then they say it back. Neither of you looks away.
What's the closest you've come tonight to just saying what you're thinking?
Guess what's making patience difficult for me tonight.~Then I tell you, and you say whether it's the same for you.
Ten uninterrupted minutes, no rules. Paint it in words.~They can't interrupt or react until you've completely finished.
Finish this out loud: 'If you asked me to stay a little longer, I'd—'
What's the tension between you two right now, if you had to describe it as weather?
Tell them the thing about their restraint that's testing yours.~Then they decide out loud whether to keep restraining.
What's a version of tonight you've already imagined that hasn't happened yet?
Say the line you've been holding back all night.~Say it once, plainly. Then stop talking for five seconds.
On three, both say the gap between what you're saying and what you're thinking.~Bigger gap goes first on the next card.
Guess where I'd want your attention next.~Then I tell you whether you're right. Words only.
What's one thing you want badly enough tonight that it's a little embarrassing to admit?
Say plainly what you want to happen in the next hour.~They give a real answer — yes, not yet, or no. 'Maybe' isn't allowed.
Notice your breathing right now and say what it's doing.~Then they say what theirs is doing. Both honest.
What's the last thing their hands did tonight that you wanted to feel instead of just watch?
Name one memory — from tonight, or from way before tonight — that this exact moment just reminded you of.
Guess what they're anticipating in the next five minutes.~Then they tell you how close you got.
Sit still for three seconds, then say what your body's doing that your face isn't.~They don't respond. They just listen.
How close would you let them get right now, if there were absolutely no reason to hold back?
What's the one word for how warm it suddenly feels? Say it — don't explain it.
Tell them exactly what it does to you when they lower their voice like that.
Guess the next card they're hoping comes up.~Then they say what they'd actually do if it did.
Name the exact spot tonight where you first stopped being able to concentrate on anything else.
What's making it hardest to sit still right now?
If they reached for your hand this second, what would you do?~Answer out loud. Nobody reaches yet.
If your hands got a vote right now, what would they want to do?
Say the thing you'd only ever text at 1am. Out loud, right now.~Then they answer it as though you had texted it.
What's a question about tonight you're dying to ask them but haven't let yourself?
Tell them what 'slow down' actually means to you right now — and whether you mean it.

3.name: Closer
3.sub: Slow, close, honest — desire with the volume up, never pressure.
q: On three, both say what changed the second this tier started. One word each.~Explanations after, not before.
Say the truest thing you're thinking about them this second.~They aren't allowed to respond for ten seconds. Let it land.
Tell them one thing about wanting someone that you don't say until it's exactly like this.
Guess what they feel more confident about tonight because of you.~Then they tell you. Take it properly, no deflecting.
Finish this out loud: 'What I want, if I'm honest, is—' (Words only — say it, don't act on it yet.)
Both name what you wanted an hour ago, then what you want now. On three.~If the answer moved, say exactly when.
What's something about wanting someone that surprised you about yourself tonight?
Tell them what it does to you when they look at you like that.~They hold the look while you say it.
Say the bravest true thing you haven't said yet — or say you're not ready.~Both are complete answers. They don't get to push.
Name one place tenderness and want feel exactly the same to you right now.
Guess the moment from tonight they'll replay tomorrow.~Then they tell you theirs. See whether it's the same one.
What's a version of yourself you only let them see? Describe it instead of naming it.
Wanting to be touched, or wanting to be seen. Pick one for right now — not both.~Then say why that one.
Say the thing you'd only say this close, this quiet.~At the volume it deserves. Not louder.
What's one thing you're a little scared to want out loud? Say it anyway — or don't. Skipping counts here too.
Guess what 'closer' means to them right now, in their words.~Then they tell you their version.
What's the last thought you had before this card — the one you weren't going to share?
Name the exact feeling in your chest. Not 'nervous' — the real one underneath.~They name theirs after, and it can't be yours.
What's something you want tonight that has nothing to do with going any further, if you're honest?
Tell them the one thing about this moment you don't want to end.~Then both stop talking for ten seconds.
Say 'I want you closer' without using those words.~They tell you whether it landed.
Say what you're hoping happens after the last card.~'Nothing yet' is complete, and they accept it with no follow-up.
What's one thing about wanting them that feels different tonight than it has before?
Say plainly, no joke to hide behind, why it's them you want closer tonight.~They don't get to make it easier for you.
What does it do to your breathing when they say your name like that? Describe it, don't just name it.
If your hands could do anything right now, say what they'd reach for.~Say it. Don't do it. That's the card.
What's a memory — maybe not even about them — that being this close to them just brought back?
What's one thing you haven't let yourself hope for tonight, even quietly?
Go quiet for ten full seconds. Then both say what the silence felt like, on three.
Say how much distance between you feels like too much.~Then decide together whether to close it or leave it. Either is fine.
What's the exact word for the heat in this moment — not 'hot,' the real one?
What does your voice do when you talk to them like this — softer, slower, something else? Name it.
Say one thing you'd want their hands to do, if you let yourself say it.~Words only. They just listen.
Are your hands still right now, or fidgeting — and what does that tell you?
Say one true thing about wanting them you've never said to anyone.~They aren't allowed to respond at all. It just sits there.
What's a version of 'stay' you'd actually mean tonight, if you said it?
What's the part of you that's the most present right now — not thinking ahead, not overthinking, just here?
Tell them what you were thinking in the quiet right before this card came up.
What's the truest thing your body is telling you right now that your words haven't caught up to yet?
Has tonight peaked, or is it still building? Both answer on three.~Different answers is the interesting outcome. Talk about it.

wild: Hold eye contact until one of you smiles first — no countdown, no closing your eyes to cheat.
Cup a hand to their ear and whisper one true thing about right now — something you wouldn't say at normal volume.
Rest your forehead against theirs, eyes open, for five slow breaths. Don't look away.
Press your palm flat against theirs, fingers spread, for ten seconds — no interlocking, just contact. Notice who's warmer.
Close the gap until you're sitting closer than feels strictly necessary — and stay there for the next card.
Take their hand and let it go quiet for ten seconds. Notice what that does.
Stand up, hold each other, and sway for thirty seconds with no music playing. First to hum loses.
Close your eyes. Let them trace a single word on your forearm with a fingertip — guess it before you open your eyes again.
Rest a hand over their heart for ten seconds. Say one word for what you notice.
Move in close enough to actually notice how they smell right now — and tell them, honestly, if you like it.
Kiss the back of their hand, slowly, like it's the only thing on the agenda tonight.
Match your breathing to theirs for six full breaths without telling them you're doing it — then tell them.
Hold your palm an inch from their cheek, close enough to feel the warmth, no closer, for five seconds.
Stand on opposite sides of the room. Walk toward each other at half your normal speed — no touching until you arrive.
Ask them a yes-or-no question using only your eyes and your face — no words. They answer the same way.
Write the truest compliment you've got across the back of your own hand, show it to them for three seconds, then wipe it clean.
Say their name once, quietly, like it's the only word you're allowed to use tonight — then hold five seconds of silence after.
Hold both of their hands, palms up, and trace one slow line across each palm with your fingertip — no words until you're done.
Sit back to back, shoulders touching, and describe out loud one thing you notice without being able to see them.
Trace the line of their jaw with one fingertip, slow enough they could stop you — then tell them one memory it just brought back.
Lean in like you're about to say something — then hold three full seconds before you actually say it.
Cup their face in one hand for a slow count of five, palm still, no stroking — then let go and say what you noticed.
Exhale slowly while they inhale, and swap breaths like that three times, no talking — then tell them how it felt.
Hum the first few notes of a song that reminds you of them. Don't explain why until they guess.
final: Last card. Put the phone down after this one — everything else can wait thirty seconds.
Say one true thing about tonight that you know you'll still mean tomorrow morning.
Then close the distance however feels right to you both. That's the whole rest of the game.
